$comment: GraphQL WRAPS every response under `data`, keyed by the field the document named -- `{data: {create_item: {...}}}`. Reproduced rather than flattened, because an author who wires {{ $json.data.create_item.id }} against the fake must find the same path when a real item arrives. Read from monday's introspection schema (Item: id, name, url, created_at), not from memory.

create_item.$urlComment: STATIC, and deliberately not built from the drawn id. monday's real url embeds both the board and the item -- .../boards/<boardId>/pulses/<itemId> -- and the fixture vocabulary has no concatenation, so the choice is a generic url or a made-up directive. Square's receipt_url is static for the same reason. An author reading this fake gets a plausibly-shaped link; they do not get one whose ids agree with the item beside it, and that is worth knowing before wiring a test against it.

response.$errorsComment: No `errors` key at all. GraphQL omits it on success rather than sending an empty array, and a faker that always included one would teach the wrong shape -- an author checking `if (errors)` would find it truthy on every fake call.
